cohort: The study included 126 pregnant patients with severe preeclampsia who underwent cesarean section.
finding: Combined spinal-epidural anesthesia (CSEA) significantly improved maternal hemodynamics, shortened anesthesia onset time, reduced intraoperative blood loss, increased newborn Apgar scores, and decreased postoperative adverse reactions compared to total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA).
mod_finding: Combined spinal-epidural anesthesia (CSEA) for cesarean sections in severe preeclampsia patients resulted in better maternal hemodynamics and higher newborn Apgar scores compared to total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA).
